article_text:
When Elizabeth Debicki arrived on set for “ Wicker ,” the first thing she saw was Alexander Skarsgård wading through water — full-frontal. But it wasn’t Skarsgård in the flesh; he was “stark naked as wicker.”

“I turned the corner, and I was like, ‘Hi, Alex!’ and I went bright red because my brain couldn’t compute what it was seeing,” Debicki tells Variety , sitting alongside Skarsgård and their co-star Olivia Colman in a hotel suite at the Chateau Marmont in L.A. “I was just like ‘Oh my God! Welcome to Budapest, I guess.’”

Related Stories

Christy Carlson Romano Says Her Salary Was Half of Shia LaBeouf's on 'Even Stevens': 'We Were Co-Leads and Had the Same Screen Time'

From married filmmakers Eleanor Wilson and Alex Huston Fischer, “Wicker” follows the relationship between an ostracized fisherwoman (Colman) and her fantastical husband (Skarsgård), who is handcrafted for her by the local basket weaver (Peter Dinklage). When the wicker husband proves to be a better man and partner than the rest of the married men in the village, jealousy erupts, and the unlikely couple must figure out how to preserve their simple life amid the chaos and vitriol. (And yes, Straw-Skarsgård is on full display in the Black Bear film, now playing in theaters.)

Popular on Variety

While Debicki needed a moment to grapple with the sight of a naked wicker man, Colman’s reaction mirrored her character falling in love at first sight.

“It was amazing because we’d all been looking at images for 18 months or so, and then to see it in the flesh, it was amazing,” Colman said. “That [feeling] of, ‘Oh my god, it’s going to work!’

The Oscar winner was the first to see Skarsgård in his full wicker suit and prosthetic makeup. The prototype had been sculpted after Skarsgård’s features, but when the Weta Workshop artists tried it on someone else in New Zealand, it almost worked, but not quite.

“If it doesn’t quite work, it looks like a horror film because it looks like you cut someone’s face off and glued it onto your own, and that wasn’t quite the tone we wanted to go for here,” Skarsgård explains. “So, it was a lot of anticipation and excitement and a lot of nerves because it was like, ‘Oh shit! If it doesn’t work, then we’re kind of screwed.”

Thankfully, Colman’s exuberant reaction eased any of Skarsgård’s fears. “It was an incredible day that I’ll never forget. Putting it on and then it helped me find the physicality of the character and then stepping out of the trailer and having Olivia outside going [gasps],” he recalls. “You can see how intricate and how beautiful the work was, and the fact that once it was glued onto my face, it actually moved with my movements. It’s even better than we imagined.”

The cast’s multilayered reaction is exactly what moviegoers can expect when watching “Wicker.” The film is intended to warm your heart and make you laugh, but it’s also guaranteed to make you blush. Audiences got their first peek at the film with a steamy three-minute trailer filled with sexual innuendo and hard-as-wood jokes. Since then, the marketing for the Black Bear film has taken on a life of its own, with playful promotional products like hand-woven nipple pasties, a popcorn bucket shaped like the wicker man’s torso and splinter removal kits.

But the film itself dares to go much deeper. “It’s not just a slapstick or sex comedy,” Skarsgård says. “They did an amazing job with this, and I hope and think and believe that people will go on this journey, be excited with all the twists and turns.”

In an era of box-office unpredictability, the “Wicker” cast isn’t worried about moviegoers embracing the film’s big swing. The stars believe the fanciful romance’s originality is enough to attract moviegoers to the theater — as evidenced by the post-trailer buzz. “Wicker” captured fifth place with $5.75 million from 1,471 locations, a “strong start” for the low-budget indie, according to Variety ‘s Rebecca Rubin. (Black Bear acquired the movie for $2.5 million after it generated buzz at Sundance Film Festival earlier this year.)

Colman: That was all in El and Al’s [Eleanor Wilson and Alex Huston Fischer’s] beautiful script. They just got the tone. So, you just had to follow it, and you couldn’t really go wrong. It can be hard to go from very silly to really heartbreaking, but because it was all done with realism, it worked better.

In my saddest moments in my life, I’ve definitely found myself laughing hysterically as well, which is a very human thing, pain and recovery, all those things. And El and Al just nailed it. It made our journey, our job easier.

Colman: Think wisely. Hopefully, the love you choose enhances your life, not diminishes it.

Debicki: It’s such a beautiful examination of the idea that loving someone is really looking in a mirror of yourself. You know that’s what’s so frightening. But I always think of the line when Olivia said, “Well, what does he know about love?” And the basket maker says, “Well, I imagine he learned it from you.” That’s what we do in life. We are constantly learning from each other. It’s also a really beautiful examination of the institution of marriage.

And a lot of this film is looking at what patriarchy does to women, the messaging of women needing to compete. That there’s a kind of scarcity complex that you must do it this way, and she rethinks the system and creates it in the image of herself that’s authentic, and in that she thrives, and that’s a really good conversation to have for women.”

Colman: I think people are excited about something that’s original and different. I think audiences get patronized a bit like, “Oh, they like that film. We’ll do another five like that,” and there’s space for that. But there’s also space for something totally original and different. And El and Al had control of this.

Skarsgård: The fact that they did have complete creative control and they could have the freedom to make their own movie the way they wanted to make, without lots of chefs in the kitchen or with lots of nervous financiers being like, “Well, are we sure this is going to work?” It was really exciting to be part of that journey. Like we’re making something quite unique here. There’s freedom in that.

Debicki: We’re in a very difficult time for women. If you look at women in this country and patriarchal systems, a woman’s right to choose what they do with their bodies, and how they live their lives, and just pay disparity in general since the dawn of time. I mean, women rightfully are questioning things, and this movie is refreshing because it’s looking at these issues in a way that’s really accessible and entertaining, but there’s some serious conversations in this movie. I think it’s important to talk about that.

Skarsgård: We got a splinter removal kit. And those 3D-printed wicker husband torsos. They’re popcorn buckets, and then you fill them with popcorn, popcorn out of like a wicker basket.

Skarsgård: We have a good one.

Colman: 50 Shades of Hay.

Skarsgård: It’s been a lot of fun watching this. We all love the film and were very excited when the trailer came out, but you never ever expect that kind of reaction. I’ve never had a movie with that kind of reaction. It’s been really thrilling, and we’re excited to now share the whole movie, more than just those three minutes, with the world.

article_text:
French giant Gaumont is launching a new 4K restoration of Louis Malle ‘s 1958 classic crime thriller “Elevator to the Gallows,” starring Jeanne Moreau .

Set to begin at the end of the year, the new restoration will be released in celebration of the 70th anniversary of the French New Wave, the upcoming 70th anniversary of the film in 2028 and, in the same year, the centenary of Moreau’s birth.

Related Stories

Andy Cohen Celebrates 20 Years of ‘Real Housewives’ With New Book Featuring 600 Never-Before-Seen Photos and Behind-the-Scenes Stories

Peacock App Launches 'Your Bravoverse,' Featuring a Personalized TikTok-Style Video Feed Hosted by AI-Generated Andy Cohen

Released 1958, “Elevator to the Gallows” marked the directorial debut for the young Malle, who was 25 years old at the time.

Set in Paris over the course of a night, the film stars Moreau and Maurice Ronet as lovers who set out to murder her husband and his boss (played by Jean Wall), only for the plan to go awry. Distinguished by Miles Davis’ award-winning jazz score, the film established both Malle and Moreau as verifiable talents.

Popular on Variety

Another Gaumont classic, “Betty Blue,” Jean-Jacques Beineix’s iconic tale of amour fou run rampant, is making its long-awaited return to the big screen at this year’s Lumière Film Festival in Lyon.

Originally released in 1986 as “37°2 le matin,” the award-winning erotic drama chronicles the doomed romance between Zorg (Jean-Hugues Anglade), a handyman and aspiring writer in his 30s, and the volatile, impulsive and fragile 19-year-old Betty (Béatrice Dalle).

The film is also one of this year’s highlights for Gaumont, which is presenting the new 4K master of the full 185-minute version — “a film that has been invisible in theaters in this version since 1991,” noted Jérôme Soulet, head of catalogue at Gaumont.

Gaumont is considering a theatrical release next year of the two versions of “Betty Blue,” the 1986 two-hour original and the 1991 three-hour extended version.

The extended cut presented at three screenings at the Lumière Festival will also screen in November as part of French cinema operator UGC’s UGC Culte Selection showcase, offering cinemagoers the opportunity to “(re)discover on the big screen” timeless or recent films that have marked the history of cinema and masterpieces by the greatest directors.

The 4K restoration of “Betty Blue” was carried out by Gaumont at the GP Archives laboratory.

The film screens this year as part of the Lumière Festival’s Big Films on the Big Screen sidebar that offers the opportunity to rediscover cinematic masterpieces in their intended format.

Soulet will also be on hand at the Lumière Festival’s International Classic Film Market in Lyon to present the company’s lineup of new releases at the annual Catalogue Holders’ Premiere Presentation on Wednesday.

article_text:
The Santa Barbara International Film Festival has announced the recipients of the 2027 Virtuosos Award. The award acknowledges talent whose work in films has placed them at the center of the conversation around the year’s most noteworthy cinematic performances. Carrie Coon, Mariana di Girolamo, Rosalind Eleazar, Jordan Firstman , Anthony Ippolito, Jaafar Jackson , Inde Navarrette and Kate O’Flynn are this year’s honorees. The group will attend the 42nd annual event to receive the award and discuss their work on Feb. 7.

Related Stories

Here's How to Watch WWE Money in the Bank 2026 Live Online

WWE Enters Microdrama Space With 'Agent of Shadows,' Drew McIntyre Takes Central Role

“This year’s Virtuosos are a powerhouse group from the most talked-about films of the season. I think it’s especially fitting that so many of them are international performers, and I can’t wait to help welcome them all to Santa Barbara,” Turner Classic Movies host and SBIFF moderator Dave Karger said.

Coon will be honored for her role in “The Liberation”; Mariana di Girolamo for “Wild Horse Nine”; Rosalind Eleazar for “Misty Green”; Jordan Firstman for “Club Kid”; Anthony Ippolito for “I Play Rocky”; Jaafar Jackson for “Michael”; Inde Navarrette for “Obsession”; Kate O’Flynn for “Tender Loving Care.”

Honorees over the last six years include Jacob Elordi, Chase Infiniti, Zendaya, Sydney Sweeney, Andrew Scott, Austin Butler, Renate Reinsve, Kieran Culkin, Harris Dickinson and many more.

The festival will take place from Feb. 3 to 13. Official events, including screenings, filmmaker Q&As, industry panels and celebrity tributes, will be held throughout the city, including at the Arlington Theatre and the recently opened SBIFF Film Center. Recently announced tributes include John Malkovich for the Outstanding Performer of the Year Award and Andrew Garfield for the Maltin Modern Master Award.

article_text:
“Ria,” Philippines filmmaker Arvin Belarmino ’s debut feature about a young woman from the folk-punk scene who takes on a property developer to save her home, has been picked up by international sales company Lights On following its world premiere at the Busan International Film Festival .

The film picked up the Heart of Eurasia Award after bowing in Busan.

In the story, Ria teams up with her foster mother and their fellow punks to resist a merciless developer intent on tearing down their building. It is the last structure left standing in a neighborhood that has already been reduced to rubble.

Related Stories

Meghan Markle 'Deeply Distressed' by Allegations Her Father Possessed Child Sex Abuse Images

'SNL U.K.' Cold Open Sees Reunion Between Prince William and Kate and Prince Harry and Meghan (With Some Help From Former Prince Andrew): 'They Must Want Us to Be Royals Again!'

The film is a co-production between the Philippines, the Netherlands, Saudi Arabia, Japan and Norway.

“An ode to rebellion and a fierce cry against injustice, ‘Ria’ is a film that reminds us of cinema’s ability to resist, question, and confront the world around us. A film that deserves to travel far and connect with audiences across borders,” said Lights On co-founder and managing director Flavio Armone.

Armone said the company was especially proud to see the project come together because it extends its relationship with Belarmino. The two previously worked together on “Agapito,” a Cannes-debuting short that Belarmino co-directed with Kyla Romero.

“I’m so happy to be collaborating with Lights On. They’ve been part of my journey as a filmmaker, witnessing my growth from my short film to now bringing my feature film to life. There’s something so fulfilling about finding people who see your vision, believe in your stories, and grow alongside you,” said Belarmino.

Producer Kristine De Leon said making the film had not been easy, adding: “Having people you can trust makes the journey a little lighter. That’s something I’ve found with Lights On.”

Lights On’s slate also includes Polen Ly’s Cambodian feature “Becoming Human,” a 2025 Venice title, and “Hair, Paper, Water…,” from Nicolas Graux and Trương Minh Quý, which played Locarno the same year. “Becoming Human” is Cambodia’s Oscar submission this year.

News

Mamdani Votes Early at The Met. What Other NYC Museums Are Polling Sites?

"It only took five minutes," said the NYC mayor in a social media video. More museums and cultural institutions across the city serve as early voting sites.

YouTube )

As New Yorkers line up to cast their midterm ballots early through Sunday, November 1, and others prepare to brave the crowds next Tuesday, November 3, some cultural institutions and museums are turning into voting sites.

"Only in New York City can you vote in places like the Metropolitan Museum of Art," Mayor Zohran Mamdani reminded viewers in an Instagram video today, October 26, while weaving through The Met's Michael C. Rockefeller Wing at the Manhattan institution. "I just voted here on the first day of early voting. It only took five minutes."

Along with hundreds of public schools, community centers, libraries, and other city gathering spaces, several museums are opening their doors for early voters. The American Museum of Natural History in Manhattan will welcome early voters through its 77th Street entrance, according to a banner on its website . Since the 2024 election cycle, the museum has set up voting stations on the first floor of the building for easy accessibility.

Across Central Park, The Met returns as an early voting site after serving as one for multiple past general elections and the primaries this June. The Brooklyn Museum, another longtime venue for elections, will also be open for early voting.

Cellophane

“Cellophane” is a visual investigation into the boundaries of memory and identity, exploring how our minds fragment and preserve parts of our lives. Moving between dream and reality through subtle chiaroscuro, the series seeks an interpretation for a past that remains in the shadows, treating light and shadow as membranes between who we were and who we are now.

article_text:
ＳＯＭＰＯ美術館（東京都新宿区）から、2027年度の展覧会スケジュールが発表されました。

2027年度は、「描かれたモード ―フランス女性の新時代（仮称）」「テクノロジー×アートの扉」「画家たちのバルビゾン―海を越えた風景のダイアローグ」「写真と建築（仮称）」「FACE展2028／絵画のゆくえ2028」と、全部で5つの展覧会が予定されています。19世紀から現代に至る絵画やモード、写真、最先端のメディアアート、そして公募展まで、多彩な切り口で美の諸相に迫る充実のラインアップとなっています。

そこでここまで判明した各展覧会の概要について、それぞれまとめました。

ＳＯＭＰＯ美術館

所在地：東京都新宿区西新宿1-26-1

開館時間：10:00～18:00 ※入館は閉館の30分前まで （※展覧会により変更となる場合があります）

休館日：月曜日（祝休日の場合は開館）、展示替期間、年末年始

観覧料：展覧会ごとに異なります。詳細は公式サイトをご確認ください

アクセス： JR・私鉄・地下鉄各線 新宿駅西口より徒歩5分 都営大江戸線 都庁前駅A1出口より徒歩6分 東京メトロ丸ノ内線 西新宿駅より徒歩8分

詳細は、 ＳＯＭＰＯ美術館公式サイト まで。

描かれたモード―フランス女性の新時代（仮称）

2027年4月24日～6月27日

時代とともに変化したモード（ファッション）は、社会を映す鏡といえます。本展覧会は19世紀半ばから20世紀初頭まで、フランスを中心とする美術作品に描かれたモードの変遷をたどり、第二帝政期からベル・エポックを経て、第一次世界大戦後の「狂乱の時代」まで、各時代を生きた女性たちの姿が紹介されます。油彩、版画（ポスター）が出品される予定です。

テクノロジー×アートの扉

2027年7月17日～8月29日

AIが暮らしに浸透する現代、テクノロジーを用いて心躍る体験や気づきをもたらすアートが紹介されます。本展では、光や動き、インタラクションなど、2000年代以降の作品から現在の若手作家まで、多彩な手法による約14点が登場。光と影が生み出す世界の中には、初期のビデオゲームや幻燈などを想起させる作品も。驚きや実感を味わううちに、ふと哲学的な思いに導かれるような、感性と知的好奇心を刺激する展覧会です。

画家たちのバルビゾン―海を越えた風景のダイアローグ

2027年9月18日～12月12日

スコットランド国立美術館の優れたバルビゾン派コレクションを中心に、日本国内所蔵作品を加えた油彩、素描、版画、写真によって、19世紀フランス近代風景画の展開に焦点が当てられます。展示では、英国とフランス風景画の相互の影響にも着目し、バルビゾン派誕生前夜の動向から、コローやミレーらを中心とする同派の多彩な表現をたどります。さらに、印象派から19世紀後半の英国風景画までを視野に収め、バルビゾン派を中心とする近代風景画の豊かな系譜が展観されます。

写真と建築（仮称）

2028年1月8日～2月20日

本展は、写真の発明まもない19世紀から20世紀のモダニズムまで、建築や都市が写真によってどのように記録され、分析され、イメージ化されてきたかをたどります。写真は、建物の外観を写すだけでなく、そこに刻まれた人びとの暮らしや記憶、社会の変化をも伝えてきました。建築を通して都市や時代を見つめてきた、写真の役割が紹介されます。

FACE展2028／絵画のゆくえ2028

2028年3月4日～3月26日

第16回目となる平面作品の公募展です。「年齢・所属を問わない新進作家の登竜門」として、全国より応募された作品から入選・受賞した約60点を展示し、観覧者投票によるオーディエンス賞も授与されます。

また、前回のFACE2027でグランプリと優秀賞を受賞した作家を招待する「絵画のゆくえ2028」が3階展示室に併設され、各作家の新作・近作も5～10点ずつ取り上げられます。さまざまな技法やモチーフで時代の感覚をとらえた作品を楽しんでみてはいかがでしょうか。

2027年度のＳＯＭＰＯ美術館は、激動の時代を生きた女性たちとモードの変遷を見つめる展覧会から、最先端のテクノロジーとアートが織りなす体感型の企画、さらにスコットランド国立美術館の至宝でたどるバルビゾン派の風景画、都市と人々の記憶を写し出す建築写真展、そして未来を担う新進気鋭の画家たちによる公募展まで、時代も表現形式も越えた魅力的なプログラムが揃いました。季節ごとに表情を変える多彩な名品との出合いを心待ちに、ぜひ足繁く通ってみてはいかがでしょうか。（美術展ナビ）

article_text:
ON SEEING 2026 WITH JAMIE MAXTONE-GRAHAM

Dates: From April to June 2026

Venue: Matca Space for Photography, 48 Ngoc Ha, Ba Dinh, Hanoi

Language: English

Tuition-free

Limited to 10 participants

Register before 08.03.2026 via Google Form

On Seeing 2026 with Jamie Maxtone-Graham is a three-month photography workshop, designed for experienced photographers who have a specific project proposal in mind and wish to work in a small, dedicated group with like-minded practitioners. Led by Jamie Maxtone-Graham and taking place at Matca Space for Photography, the workshop is tuition-free and hosts up to 10 participants selected via the open call.

The workshop is open to Vietnamese photographers working in all aspects of the medium (editorial, personal, experimental, artistic, etc.) looking to elevate their practice to the next level. The only requirement is full commitment to the creative process and the development of a self-driven portfolio on a theme of choice. Chosen participants are expected to move forward with their projects and attend weekly group critiques. Meetings will focus on updating progress, presenting research, sharing ideas for overcoming creative and technical challenges, and refining strategies toward the completion of each participant’s project. The workshop will be conducted in English with some accommodation for those with limited proficiency.

Planned to take place from April to June 2026, sessions will be held weekly in the evenings or on weekends. Further details will be shared with chosen participants.

How to apply

To apply, please send the following before March 08, 2026 via Google Form :

A link to previous work

A description of the photographic series you would like to develop

CV and other relevant documents (optional)

The result will be announced via email on March 15, 2026. Some candidates might be contacted for an interview.

About the organizer

Jamie Maxtone-Graham is a photographer and filmmaker with a long history of producing personal photography portfolios and conducting intensive, long-term photography workshops at both Hanoi DocLab and Matca. Previous attendees have used their completed portfolios to apply to other regional workshops and residencies (Angkor Photo Workshops, Objectifs, Nha San Collective, San Art, etc.), join in group and solo local and international exhibitions, and major awards and grant submissions (Prince Claus Fund’s Seed Award, Aperture, etc.).

FAQs

1. What is an “experienced” photographer? Am I eligible if I’m still a student?

Students are especially encouraged to apply. “Experienced” simply means you have at least one complete body of work that represents your visual thinking or interests.

2. What kind of photographs should I include in my portfolio?

The photographs in your portfolio should contain the concerns and ideas you are most interested in and reflect your delight in seeing.

3. I cannot be in Hanoi for the whole workshop duration. Can I still apply?

This workshop is best experienced in person, and people who cannot be present for the entire period should inform the organizer upon application. While all are welcome to apply, priority will be given to those who can commit fully.

4. What are the selection criteria?

Selection will be based on past works in conjunction with the current proposal. Short-listed applicants will be interviewed.

5. How is the three-month workshop structured?

Week to week, the workshop will respond to the needs of the group. In general, this is a critique-based workshop where during each class, ongoing student work is displayed and discussed, receiving feedback from classmates and the organizer. Visiting artists will also share work and experience, and students will conduct their own research and in-class presentations. The workshop will culminate in students presenting their finished portfolios.

editorial_excerpt_zh: 在介绍与九州有渊源的美术家的熊本市现代美术馆Gallery Ⅲ，将举办出身于大分、现居广岛的谏山元贵（1987年—）的个展。谏山一直以“复制与崩解”这一主题为轴心，通过影像和立体作品，对现代社会的合理化所带来的大量生产、规格化及可交换性进行批判 View More > The post GⅢ-Vol.167 Dolly ( ) 谏山元贵 first appeared on ART iT（アートイット） .
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "image", "url": "https://www.art-it.asia/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/3_1080×1080px（正方形）表.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "ART iT · 日本語", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在介绍与九州有渊源的美术家的熊本市现代美术馆Gallery Ⅲ，将举办出身于大分、现居广岛的谏山元贵（1987年—）的个展。谏山一直以“复制与崩解”这一主题为轴心，通过影像和立体作品，对现代社会的合理化所带来的大量生产、规格化及可交换性进行批判。在用模具复制出的泥土物体于水中崩解的影像作品中，他以速度无编辑的形式展现了这种无法控制的变化过程。衰老与崩解，以及附着于其上的时间，是否能让我们找到原创性的所在之处——。谏山的这一追问，最终引导他走向了位于生命与物件之间的“克隆羊多莉”（羊のドリー）。多莉是1996年在英国诞生的世界上第一只利用体细胞出生的哺乳动物克隆体。孕育多莉的技术虽然包含着伦理问题，但也开启了后来再生医疗发展等大门，带来了希望。在距离诞生迎来30周年这一节点之际，本展旨在通过以多莉为题材的作品，重新思考生命的复制技术与物象化及其伦理的、社会的意义。在静静崩解的谏山的多莉彼岸，我们究竟能看到什么？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "1996年7月5日，克隆羊多莉在苏格兰罗斯林研究所诞生，今年迎来了30周年。当时，我正在阅读手冢治虫的《火之鸟·生命篇》（1980年）。这部作品将克隆人作为主题之一。现在依然，不，正因为是现在，我对其中描绘的人类“物化”——人类被当作 mono（物件），或者被当作一个 Object（客体）对待——感到了犹如创伤般的恐惧。围绕多莉的诞生，我认为对于催生或试图催生它的技术，需要某种伦理。但是，诞生出来的存在本身并没有罪。正因如此，我想对多莉由衷地说一声“恭喜”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "艺术家简介 谏山元贵 (いさやま・げんき) 1987年出生。美术家。2014年作为吉野石膏美术振兴财团海外研修资助学者驻留柏林，参加Studio Haegue Yang的驻留项目。主要展览包括：“收藏展 2025-Ⅱ”（含特邀作品）/ “谏山元贵：万物的次第”（广岛市现代美术馆，2025）、「Dolly」（hakari contemporary，京都，2024，策展人：鹈尾佳奈）、MOMAS 收藏Ⅲ期 (特邀作品)（埼玉县立近代美术馆，2023）、「Each Day Begins with the Sun Rising」（波莫纳学院本顿艺术博物馆，加利福尼亚，2022）、「高松当代艺术年展 vol.11」（高松市美术馆，香川，2022）、「远距风景」（Art Gallery Miyauchi，广岛，2017）、「Sights and Sounds:Japan」（犹太博物馆，纽约，2016）等。主要作品被广岛市现代美术馆、波莫纳学院本顿艺术博物馆、高松市美术馆等收藏。主要奖项有“VOCA展 2025”鼓励奖、“第2届广岛文化新人奖”（2021）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展览信息 GⅢ-Vol.167 Dolly ( ) 谏山元贵 展览会期：2026年10月31日（周六）—12月27日（周日） 开馆时间：10:00 — 20:00 休馆日：周二（11月3日开馆）、11月4日 会场：Gallery Ⅲ・井手宣通纪念美术馆 观展费：免费 主办：熊本市现代美术馆（熊本市、公益财团法人熊本市美术文化振兴财团） 鸣谢：hakari contemporary（株式会社基住）、Art Gallery Miyauchi", "translated": true}]

article_text:
九州ゆかりの美術家を紹介する熊本市現代美術館のギャラリーⅢにて、大分出身の諫山元貴（1987年～／広島在住）の個展を開催します。 諫山はこれまで「複製と崩壊」というテーマを軸に、現代社会の合理化がもたらす大量生産・規格化・交換可能性を、映像や立体作品によって批評してきました。型を用いて複製された土の物体が水の中で崩壊していく映像作品では、その制御できない変化の様子を、速度無編集で提示しています。衰えや崩壊、そこに付帯する時間に、オリジナリティの在り処を見出せるのではないか――。 諫山のこの問いは、やがて生命とモノとの間に位置する“羊のドリー”へと導かれました。ドリーは、1996年イギリスで、世界で初めて成体細胞を用いて生まれたクローンの哺乳類です。ドリーを生んだ技術は倫理的な問題を孕みながらも、その後の再生医療の発展といった扉を開け、希望ももたらしています。誕生から30年という節目に、本展はドリーを題材とした作品を通して、生命の複製技術と物象化、その倫理的・社会的意味について再考する場をめざします。静かに崩れゆく諫山のドリーのむこうに、私たちは何を見ることができるのでしょうか。

1996年7月5日、クローン羊ドリーがスコットランドのロスリン研究所で誕生してから、今年で30周年を迎える。当時、私は手塚治虫の『火の鳥―生命編』（1980年）を読んでいた。この作品はクローン人間を主題のひとつとして扱っている。今でも、いや、今だからこそ、そこに描かれた人間の「モノ化」―人間が mono として、あるいはひとつの Object として扱われること―に、トラウマのような恐怖を覚える。 ドリーの誕生をめぐっては、それを生み出した、あるいは生み出そうとする技術に対して、何らかの倫理が求められると考えている。しかし、生まれてきた存在そのものに罪はない。 だからこそ、ドリーには素直に「おめでとう」と言いたい。

作家プロフィール 諫山元貴 (いさやま・げんき) 1987年生まれ。美術家。2014年吉野石膏美術振興財団在外研修助成にてベルリンに滞在、Studio Haegue Yang のレジデンスプログラムに参加。主な展覧会に、「コレクション展 2025-Ⅱ」（特別出品含む）/ 「諫山元貴：ものの次第」（ 広島市現代美術館、2025）、「Dolly」（hakari contemporary、京都、2024、キュレーター：鵜尾佳奈）、MOMAS コレクションⅢ期 (特別出品) 」 (埼玉県立近代美術館、2023) 、「Each Day Begins with the Sun Rising」（Benton Museum of Art Pomona College、カリフォルニア、2022）、「高松コンテンポラリーアート・アニュアル vol.11」 (高松市美術館、香川、2022)、「テレポーティング・ランドスケープ」（アートギャラリーミヤウチ、広島、2017）、「Sights and Sounds:Japan」(ユダヤ博物館、ニューヨーク、2016)、など。主な作品収蔵先に広島市現代美術館、ポモナ大学付属ベントン美術館、高松市美術館などがある。主な受賞に「VOCA展 2025」奨励賞、「第２回広島文化新人賞」（2021） 。

article_text:
PATRICK CHUKA

A BOOKPRJECT BY CHU

Chu is a Nigerian-American creative and technologist building meaningful experiences from Los Angeles.

I left Lagos at 17 with nothing but talent and determination. Nine years later, I’ve built an artistic practice featured in BBC, exhibited internationally, and lead AI systems engineering at a marketing technology company.

Art taught me patience. Code taught me scale. Both taught me that the best work happens when you refuse to choose between beauty and function.

Afrophilia-X: The Scapegoat That Grew Wings blends ballpoint pen portraiture with autobiographical fiction, exploring African identity, exile, and transformation. It took five years to create. Website: https://patrickchuka.com Book: https://afrophilia-x.shop

editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "在安格斯·麦克拉克伦（Angus MacLachlan）的《小祈祷》（A Little Prayer）中，大卫·斯特雷泽恩（David Strathairn）的表演没有一个镜头、没有一句台词、没有一个动作流露出丝毫雕琢的痕迹。麦克拉克伦最为人熟知的作品是编剧了广受赞誉的《六月虫》（2005），他一直默默耕耘着自己的导演生涯，拍摄了一部部质朴却深情、融入了其剧作家经历并浸润着其家乡北卡罗来纳州温斯顿-塞勒姆质感的电影。他挖掘世俗与家庭琐事却不搞夸张的情节剧，这或许就是为什么他的作品往往会被那些追求火爆场面的影迷所忽视。在这位导演身上，斯特雷泽恩找到了最完美的缪斯，这位演员的巨大价值历来在于他那种能够安于当下的朴素能力。76岁的斯特雷泽恩饰演比尔（Bill）——一位年迈的越战老兵，面对自己那个误入歧途、酗酒成性的儿子以及饱受折磨的儿媳那四分五裂的生活，他不知该如何插手。斯特雷泽恩成功避开了饰演家长时所有生俱来的陷阱：既没有刻意表现出的凝重，也没有老态龙钟地博取观众的同情。他极为感人的表演提醒着人们，伟大的表演往往源自演员日积月累的丰富阅历，而非刻意为之的“沉浸”。斯特雷泽恩饰演的比尔无疑在大半生里都生活在这个地方、这个街区。面对生活中的种种失意，他是一个令人完全信服、具有当代小津安二郎风格的笠智众。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "虽然斯特雷泽恩深思熟虑的表演与麦克拉克伦不着痕迹的人文主义节奏完美契合，但80岁的凯瑟琳·查尔方特（Kathleen Chalfant）在莎拉·弗里德兰（Sarah Friedland）的《熟悉的触摸》（Familiar Touch）中细腻的主演表现，堪称演员如何提升周围剧本水准的教学级范例。她饰演出生于布鲁克林的鲁斯·戈德曼（Ruth Goldman），一位开始出现记忆减退并正在适应护理机构生活的退休职业厨师。身为戏剧界老将的查尔方特目标明确且迷人，当她试图向一位新医生狂热地背诵罗宋汤的菜谱时，这种魅力达到了顶点：她坚持要用红葡萄酒和香醋来代替苹果醋时的喜悦；她命令必须“只放一小撮！”香菜籽时的狂热；以及当她一时把生菜错当成卷心菜时的懊恼！尽管《Familiar Touch》延续了电影戏剧化刻画痴呆症的套路（这种次类型本质上是虚假的，因为它假定能对一种不可知的疾病进行内部剖析，却又往往流于陈词滥调和关于记忆的空灵隐喻），并且回避了高端养老护理机构中根深蒂固的阶级与种族等令人不安的问题，但查尔方特赋予了鲁斯对人际连接的热切渴望。尽管她的现实正在消逝，但过去在她充满福气的脸庞上始终清晰可见。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "另一位技压全场的资深演员是75岁的艾米·马迪根（Amy Madigan），她为扎克·克雷格（Zach Cregger）大肆张扬的恐怖片热作《武器》（Weapons）提供了冰冷的内核。这部电影浪费了一个绝佳的前提，本可借此探讨当代人对儿童福祉的焦虑以及美国父母试图保护孩子所带来的狂热，却最终呈现为一场哗众取宠的惊悚之旅。然而不知为何，片中最令人失望的情节揭晓（噢，原来一直是个女巫）却激发出了它最具有观赏性的元素：邪恶女巫格拉迪斯阿姨（Aunt Gladys），一个真正可怕的角色，由马迪根以全情投入、令人作呕的激情将其演活了。尽管我是她这种独特风格的长期粉丝，但在电影进行了一半时我甚至没认出她来。马迪根对伤感极其排斥（即便在《梦幻成真》（1989）这样催泪的电影中也是如此），她走向完全的反派角色只是时间问题。抛开一桶桶的血浆不谈，难以捉摸的马迪根在片中流露出了脆弱的时刻。马迪根、查尔方特和斯特雷泽恩的表演共同凝聚了一种自信的不伤感；看着他们的表演，我感到无比踏实，因为我绝不会被强迫去作出过度的同理心、同情或恐惧反应。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
There isn’t a scene, there isn’t a line, there isn’t a single gesture in which David Strathairn pushes into the realm of artifice in Angus MacLachlan’s A Little Prayer. MacLachlan, best known for writing the precious Junebug (2005), has quietly been forging a directorial career of unprepossessing but soulful films, informed by his work as a playwright and imbued with the texture of his hometown of Winston-Salem, North Carolina. He mines matters of the mundane and the domestic without histrionics, which is perhaps why his work tends to go unnoticed by moviegoers looking for fireworks. In Strathairn, the director has found his perfect muse, an actor whose great value has always resided in his simple ability to be present. As Bill, an aging Vietnam War veteran confused about how far to insert himself into the fracturing lives of his wayward, alcoholic son and long-suffering daughter-in-law, the 76-year-old Strathairn avoids every innate pitfall in playing the patriarch: there’s neither studied gravitas nor doddering angling for the audience’s commiseration. His enormously touching work is a reminder that great performances often emanate from an actor’s accrued experience rather than self-conscious “immersion.” Strathairn’s Bill has undoubtedly existed in this place, this neighborhood, for most of his adulthood. Facing life’s disappointments, he’s a wholly convincing latter-day Chishû Ryû.

While Straithairn’s thoughtful work matches MacLachlan’s unforced humanism beat for beat, 80-year-old Kathleen Chalfant’s delicate starring turn in Sarah Friedland’s Familiar Touch is a master class in how a performer can elevate her surrounding material. She plays Brooklyn-born Ruth Goldman, a former professional cook starting to suffer memory loss and adjusting to life in a care facility. Theater veteran Chalfant is purposeful and mesmeric, never more so than when she tries to prove her mind’s strength to a new doctor by maniacally reciting the recipe for borscht: the delight in her insistence on red wine and balsamic over apple-cider vinegar; the fervor of her command to use “just a pinch!” of caraway seed; the frustration when she momentarily mistakes lettuce for cabbage! While Familiar Touch plays games familiar to cinematic dramatizations of dementia (an inherently false subgenre for the way it presumes interior portraiture on an unknowable disease and too often falls back on platitudes and ethereal metaphors about memory), and begs off troubling issues of class and race endemic to such high-end eldercare facilities, Chalfant imbues Ruth with a fervent desire for connection. The past is always clear on her beatific face even as her present is slipping away.

Another veteran actor outclassing the joint, 75-year-old Amy Madigan provides the ice-cold center to Zach Cregger’s flamboyant horror hit Weapons. The film squanders a fertile premise that would seem to speak to contemporary anxieties about the welfare of our children and the mania that surrounds American parents’ attempts to protect them, instead delivering a sensationalist thrill ride. Yet somehow the film’s most disappointing plot revelation (oh, it was a witch all along) coaxes out its most watchable element: the evil sorceress Aunt Gladys, a genuinely horrible creation, embodied with full, revolting gusto by Madigan, whom I didn’t recognize for half of the film despite having been a longtime fan of her idiosyncratic work. It was only a matter of time before Madigan—allergic to bathos even in tearjerkers like Field of Dreams (1989)—went full villain. Despite the buckets of gore, the unpredictable Madigan allows moments of vulnerability. A confident unsentimentality unites the work of Madigan, Chalfant, and Strathairn; watching them, I felt secure that I was never being forced to react with undue empathy, sympathy, or fear.

title_original: The Artist Who Spent Fifty Years Bringing Museum Dioramas Back to Life
editorial_title_zh: 这位艺术家花了五十年时间，让博物馆的立体模型重焕生机
editorial_excerpt_zh: 自1975年以来，杉本博司一直在拍摄美国自然历史博物馆里的立体模型。如今，他的这个系列即将画上句号。他找到自己一直在寻找的东西了吗？

"一对男女并肩走在被阳光晒得发白的沙漠中。较高的男性身影将手搭在女同伴的肩膀上，女同伴则向一侧瞥去，嘴唇微张，仿佛正准备对远处的某个新奇事物评头论足。他们似乎对背景中正在喷发火山漠不关心，如果不是赤身裸体且浑身长满长长的粗毛，他们看起来完全就像是一对在巴黎街头漫步的闲逛者。他们的面部呈类人猿状，有着浓重的眉骨、扁平的鼻子以及前突的下颌。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "杉本博司于1994年拍摄的《最早的人类亲属》是一张令人眼花缭乱的照片。乍一看，这些毛发浓密的形象似乎是戴着最新款人猿义肢的模特，在某个偏远的火山地区为艺术家摆出造型。或者他们也可能是从《2001太空漫游》中溜出来抽烟休息的群众演员。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "但有些地方又显得不太对劲。仔细观察，附近树下一群正在啄泥的鸟显得很扁平，隐约带有漫画感。更远处那群微型马也是如此。尽管我们的大脑告诉我们这些史前人物是切实存在的，但这个场景中依然有一种缺乏说服力的感觉。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "杉本博司这张神秘莫测的照片描绘了纽约美国自然历史博物馆中一个已成过往的立体模型。这些雕塑般的重构人物——来自埃塞俄比亚的南方古猿阿法种著名化石代表“露西”及其男性同伴——曾经站在一块人工泥土上，背景是一幅画作，前方则是一大块玻璃。我是伴随着这个场景长大的，对它所描绘的原始世界（以及，是的，还有那份赤裸）着迷不已。尽管极具沉浸感，但这些人物显然是雕塑，风景也只是一幅壁画。在杉本博司冷峻的镜头下，这个立体模型显得比现实中诡异得多。通过他的相机，他完成了这种幻觉。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在创作《最早的人类亲属》时，杉本博司拍摄立体模型已经将近二十年了。这个系列是这位艺术家的第一个也是最持续、最成熟的作品主体，始于1974年他搬到纽约后不久。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "虽然人们很容易想象杉本博司——他后来对科学的兴趣促使他拍摄了化石、数学模型以及棱镜的光学效应——会直接径直走向博物馆，但这并不是他的第一站。事实上，这是他在一座新城市寻找方向时所参观的众多伟大机构名单上的最后一站。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": article_text:
A couple walks side by side across a sun-bleached desert. The taller, male figure rests his hand on the shoulders of his female companion, who glances off to one side, lips parted, as though she’s about to remark on some distant curiosity. Seemingly unconcerned by the volcano erupting in the background, they might pass for a pair of flaneurs strolling the streets of Paris—if they weren’t naked and covered in long shaggy hair. Their faces are apelike, with heavy brows, flat noses, and jutting prognathic jaws.

Earliest Human Relatives (1994) by Hiroshi Sugimoto is a bewildering photograph. At first glance, it might seem as though the hirsute figures are models wearing the latest in simian prosthetics, posing for the artist in some remote volcanic region. Or they could be extras from 2001: A Space Odyssey caught sneaking off set for a cigarette break.

But something’s not quite right. The flock of birds pecking the dirt under a nearby tree looks flat and vaguely cartoonish on close inspection. So does the miniscule herd of horses even farther away. There’s something unconvincing about the scene, even as our brains tell us the prehistoric figures are tangibly real.

Sugimoto’s enigmatic photograph depicts a bygone diorama at New York’s American Museum of Natural History. The figures—sculptural reconstructions of Lucy, the famous fossil representative of Australopithecus afarensis from Ethiopia, and a male counterpart—once stood on a patch of artificial dirt, before a painted background, behind a large pane of glass. I grew up with this tableau, fascinated by the primordial world (and, yes, the nakedness) it depicted. Transporting though it was, the figures were clearly sculptures, the landscape a mural. In Sugimoto’s deadpan photograph, the diorama appears far more uncanny than it did in life. With his camera, he’s completed the illusion.

When Sugimoto made Earliest Human Relatives , he’d been photographing dioramas for nearly twenty years. The series, the artist’s first and most sustained mature body of work, began soon after he moved to New York, in 1974.

Although it’s tempting to imagine Sugimoto—whose interest in science has since led him to photograph fossils, mathematical models, and the optical effects of prisms—making an immediate beeline for the museum, it wasn’t his first stop. In fact, it was the very last on a list of great institutions he visited to find his bearings in a new city.

Aperture Magazine Subscription

And yet it was there, not in the city’s great art collections, that Sugimoto’s career began. Wandering the darkened halls of wildlife dioramas, he made a startling discovery. These displays, with their taxidermy animals, artificial plants, and painted backgrounds, looked “utterly fake” to the young artist, but when he closed one eye, simulating the way a single-lens camera perceives the world, they suddenly looked real. The seams between the three-dimensional foregrounds and painted walls became undetectable. Instead of static displays inside an urban museum, his photographs seemed to show living creatures in exotic habitats.

In 1975, Sugimoto returned to the museum with an 8-by-10-inch camera. When a security guard asked him if he had permission for the photoshoot, the artist said he did. Technically, this was true. Sugimoto had told museum officials he was a tourist and secured permission to take photographs—he’d neglected to mention he would be constructing makeshift tents around the dioramas to block reflections on the glass or that the exposures would last around twenty minutes.

Sugimoto’s desire to resurrect the lifeless animals on display is the same desire that motivated museum staff to fabricate them in the first place.

The artist photographed two dioramas on that first expedition. One depicts a rowdy flock of vultures tearing into a zebra carcass. In the other, a polar bear stands over a bloody seal on a stark expanse of ice. “My life as an artist began the moment I saw with my own eyes that I had succeeded in bringing the bear back to life on film,” he later wrote.

Sugimoto’s desire to resurrect the lifeless animals on display is the same desire that motivated museum staff to fabricate them in the first place. The dioramas were the cries of naturalists lamenting the environmental devastation of the early twentieth century.

“As civilization advances in Africa, the extinction of the elephant is being accomplished slowly but quite as surely as that of the American buffalo two generations ago,” wrote Carl Akeley, the pioneering taxidermist, big game hunter, and namesake of the museum’s Akeley Hall of African Mammals. Akeley mourned the destructive impact of Europeans and Americans on the African wilderness even though (or largely because) he’d known the continent when it was a paradise for Great White Hunters.

By presenting audiences with spectacular wild scenes, Akeley hoped to rally support for conservation among urbanites who’d likely never experience these places firsthand. Although his preservationist ideals and destructive appetites may be difficult for contemporary readers to reconcile, they weren’t paradoxical for him or the many wealthy sportsmen who championed conservation at the time.

Dioramas themselves have recently become endangered species. Few public museums could afford the costly collecting expeditions and painstaking artistry of the old dioramas today, even if they wanted to. Major institutions have even destroyed their antique dioramas in recent years, replacing them with sleeker, more modern displays equipped with touch screens, animatronics, and other whiz-bang attractions. Although the American Museum of Natural History has largely resisted this trend, Lucy and her companion barely survived a revamp that claimed their volcanic desert environment. Today, the couple stands inside a glass vitrine, surrounded by glowing screens. Over the past fifty years, Sugimoto has inadvertently created an archive of a disappearing art.

Museum staff who once bristled at Sugimoto’s claim that the dioramas look more “real” in his photographs than they do in life have since come around. “He really does, through his work, honor the dioramas as the fine art that they are,” said Stephen Quinn, an authority on dioramas who built and restored them at the museum for nearly forty years. Now, Sugimoto says, the series is almost complete. He took his last photographs at the American Museum of Natural History in the fall of 2025. How did he feel about finishing a body of work he began as a young man? “Relief,” he said, seated in his New York studio. “Fifty years is enough.”

For this final photoshoot, Sugimoto used color film—a first for the series. He returned to a diorama he shot before, in black and white, depicting a path winding through a bird sanctuary on Long Island. Although dozens of birds perch and flit through the blooming trees, in gray scale they’re difficult to spot, their bodies well camouflaged. In color, the scene resembles an Impressionist painting: a scarlet tanager, practically invisible in the earlier print, is a shock of red among the dappled patches of pink, white, and green.

Over time, Sugimoto has increasingly trained his lens on overlooked dioramas showing ecosystems devoid of central, spectacular subjects. In these serene landscapes, the artist sees prophetic visions of a posthuman world.

“Humans should be punished by nature,” Sugimoto told me recently, gesturing at a nearby window. “These skyscrapers—so unnatural.” Years ago, the artist could see the George Washington Bridge, about nine miles north of Chelsea. Now, glossy spires block the view.

Sugimoto takes comfort in the thought that humans aren’t long for this world. “Nature will survive,” he said. The artist likes to imagine vines and wild grass overtaking the natural history museum uptown, its roof collapsing on the dioramas, and even his own Odawara Art Foundation in Japan in ruins. Thousands of years from now, he says, the stones will still look beautiful.

This article originally appeared in Aperture No. 264, “Stop Time,” guest edited by Hiroshi Sugimoto.
excerpt_original: Hiroshi Sugimoto has photographed the dioramas at the American Museum of Natural History since 1975. Now his series is coming to a close. Did he find what he was looking for?
translated_title_zh: 花了五十年时间让博物馆立体模型复活的艺术家
translated_excerpt_zh: 杉本博司自 1975 年以来一直在美国自然历史博物馆拍摄立体模型。现在他的系列作品即将结束。他找到他要找的东西了吗？

title_original: Ecuadorian Queer Drama ‘Princess’ Swooped On by MMM Film Sales Ahead of Tallinn
editorial_title_zh: 厄瓜多尔酷儿剧情片《Princess》在塔林电影节前夕被 MMM Film Sales 买下
editorial_excerpt_zh: 总部位于巴黎的 MMM Film Sales 已取得厄瓜多尔电影人克里斯蒂安·罗哈斯（Christian Rojas）长片处女作《Princess》（原名《Ñusta》）的国际版权，该片即将在塔林黑夜电影节（PÖFF）举行世界首映。《Princess》入围了该电影节的处女作竞赛单元……

{"type": "paragraph", "text": "《Princess》入围了该电影节的处女作竞赛单元，讲述了来自安第斯山脉的 12 岁原住民女孩卡尔帕（Kallpa）的故事，她正为社区的节日做准备——每年节日上都会选出“纽斯塔”（ñusta，即公主）。卡尔帕梦想着参与其中，却面临一个现实：她出生时是个男孩。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "相关报道", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/MCDSORE_SP013-e1791584119615.jpg?w=250&h=167&crop=1", "alt": "THE SOCIAL Ruin’", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/film/news/bill-burr-the-social-reckoning-zuckerberg-1236907159/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这个故事探讨了她的身份寻找与性别过渡，这些与她的原住民根基、社区以及安第斯世界观紧密交织。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "综艺热门文章", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "MMM Film Sales 的马蒂亚斯·安古尔旺特（Matthias Angoulvant）表示，该片“感官丰富、独具一格的叙事手法从前几个镜头就震撼了我们。通过一个极力想要超越被强加的身份与角色的原住民儿童的眼睛和身体，影片以非凡的克制力呈现了一种亲密的痛苦。这是一部大胆、深具打动人心的酷儿处女作，体现了我们在 MMM 所倡导的胆识电影。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《Princess》由厄瓜多尔的 Epopeya 和 Oso Rojo Films 出品，并与秘鲁的 Agua Florida、阿根廷的 Hain Cine、墨西哥的 Woo Films 以及玻利维亚的 Chao Pescao 联合制作。", "links": [{"text": "Ecuador", "url": "https://variety.com/t/ecuador/"}, {"text": "Woo Films", "url": "https://variety.com/t/woo-films/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Nusta_Still1.jpg?w=1024", "alt": "", "caption": "由 Epopeya S.A. 提供", "credit": "Variety · Film", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Epopeya 的制片人玛丽亚·德洛斯·安赫莱斯·帕拉西奥斯（María de los Angeles Palacios）表示：“对我们来说，与 MMM Film Sales 的合作不仅仅是一桩商业交易，更是观念上的契合。《Ñusta》是一部细腻的电影；它从亲密的地方、从身体以及从一段被压抑的记忆中发声。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "她补充道：“像这样的一部电影不能随随便便推向市场。不同之处在于，MMM 团队理解其视角，并凭借他们的经验，知道如何在不剥离其敏感性的前提下将其推向国际市场。对于一部处女作而言，这种支持与曝光度本身同样重要。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我们一直相信这部电影会找到一个完美的初次亮相之地，说实话，塔林正是我们所期望的。今年该电影节迎来 30 周年：它诞生于 1997 年，也就是《Ñusta》故事设定的同一年。这种巧合对我们有着非常特殊的意义。一部在厄瓜多尔南部安第斯山脉奥斯特罗（Austro）拍摄的电影，能在地球另一端的爱沙尼亚举行世界首映，感觉既无比美好又充满矛盾。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "帕拉西奥斯指出，国际社会对原住民故事的兴趣多年来一直在增长，“我们对此表示欢迎。我们希望的是，这种兴趣能继续拓展，去展现原住民及其故事究竟有多么多元，每一个故事都有其独特的语言、领土和抗争，以及那些并未一直拥有发声空间的嗓音。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“《Ñusta》并不试图代表所有原住民；相反，它走近了一个寻找世界归属感的安第斯女孩的亲密故事。这部电影也是在与接纳我们的社区进行对话和建立纽带的过程中构建起来的。对我而言，电影的价值恰恰在于那种以敏感、尊重和开放的态度去接近其他现实的可能性，并认识到讲故事或生活并没有单一的方式。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "事实上，导演罗哈斯强调了厄瓜多尔原住民社会的巨大多样性：“需要指出的是，这部电影并不是关于某一个特定社区的。厄瓜多尔有超过 18 个原住民民族和 14 种原住民国籍，他们非常多元。原住民身份并不是单一的东西；它是异质的，这部电影发生在安第斯山脉，但并不是在任何特定的社区。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我们取景地位于卡尼亚尔（Cañar）的锡德锡阿内霍（Sid Sid Anejo）社区，与该社区的合作是《Ñusta》的基础。从一开始，我们就希望伸出援手、分享故事并倾听他们的意见，因为对我来说重要的是，电影来到这片土地时不应显得像个外来物，而是能通过与当地人民的相遇共同构建。最美好的事情是感受到他们带着如此多的深情、慷慨和开放来接纳这个故事。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Christian-Horizontal.png?w=1024", "alt": "", "caption": "克里斯蒂安·罗哈斯，由 Oso Rojo Films 提供", "credit": "Variety · Film", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "罗哈斯回忆说，在与社区分享这个故事后，得到的反应之一是：“这些事情确实会发生，但我们不会谈论它们。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他补充道：“所以他们决定给予支持。他们的参与远远不止于出现在镜头前：他们还参与到了幕后工作，作为剧组成员积极参与了电影的构建。他们的存在、他们的信任以及他们陪伴我们的方式，赋予了《Ñusta》一种不仅存在于剧本中的东西：一种同样诞生于那种相遇的生命力。这让我充满了无尽的感激。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我相信电影同样有责任回到那些使其成为可能的地方和人们身边。这就是为什么对我们来说非常重要的是，当我们在厄瓜多尔上映《Ñusta》时，我们能够重返锡德锡阿内霍，与社区分享这部电影。不仅是为了向他们致谢，更是因为他们也是这个故事的一部分。一想到我们能够再次聚在一起，在部分故事焕发生机的地方共同观看这部电影，我就深受触动。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "片中，年轻的卡尔帕（Kallpa）在拥抱自己原住民身份的同时，也面对着村庄居民的排挤——罗哈斯认为展现这一点至关重要。“我们不该为了过上另一种生活而放弃真实的自己。我们的身份由许多部分组成：我们的身体、肤色、根基、渴望以及我们所爱的人。所有这些部分都理应共同存在，而无需请求许可。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我还希望为更多元化的酷儿形象贡献力量，摒弃刻板印象，并认识到我们的经历各不相同，成为酷儿并非只有一种方式。原住民和原住民社群也不是同质化的现实；在他们之中，有声音、抗争和正在开辟新道路的转变历程。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "罗哈斯提到了厄瓜多尔第一个原住民 LGBTQ 组织 Chawpi Runakuna，该组织代表了国内多个社群。其杰出成员之一是原住民女同性恋活动家尼纳里·奇姆巴（Ninari Chimba），她也是影片的演员之一。“对我而言，她的声音和抗争至关重要，因为它们提醒着我们，这些现实一直存在，尽管它们往往没有获得表达的空间，”导演补充道。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "罗哈斯希望这部电影能够促进厄瓜多尔社会中较为保守的阶层对该群体的更多理解与接纳。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我希望《Ñusta》也能走进那些家庭，走进那些至今仍难以理解性异见的人心中。不是通过对抗，而是通过感同身受、通过相遇以及通过相互倾听的可能性。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我不指望每个看这部电影的人都和我持相同想法，但我希望他们能够走近卡尔帕、了解她，并跨越自身的信仰与她的故事产生共鸣，”罗哈斯补充道。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“一想到这部电影可能会在一个家庭内部开启一段对话，可能会让某人鼓起勇气去倾听他们的女儿、儿子或他们以前无法理解的身边人，我就备受触动……如果这部电影能够唤醒哪怕一个人的这种共情，我就会觉得这一路走来都是值得的。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在拍摄这部电影时，罗哈斯力求讲述的故事不仅“关于排挤与暴力，也关于温柔、渴望、身体、爱以及重获自由的可能。对我来说，《Ñusta》不仅仅关乎当一个社会拒绝某人的身份时会对这个人做些什么。它也关乎当我们找到一个以爱注视我们的人时会发生什么，关乎我们如何能毫无畏惧地栖息于自己的身体，以及当我们发现世界上有一个地方能让我们做自己时会发生什么。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "寻找合适的演员至关重要，而罗哈斯在为片中年轻主角选角时获得了成功。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“能找到库里·富埃雷斯（Kuri Fuerez）简直是个奇迹。我和选角导演尼古拉斯·雅塞尔加（Nicolás Yacelga）见了很多孩子，为卡尔帕探索了各种可能，但在库里身上我发现了一些非常特别的东西。他有着非凡的敏感度，对角色的理解力极强，且具备极高的专业素养。最终说服我的是他能够从一个非常私密的角度去理解这个故事，无需言语，仅凭一个眼神就能表达出如此丰富的内心情感。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“库里不只是在扮演卡尔帕：他设法以一种深深触动我的温柔与诚实去接近她。他诠释角色时的那种方式非常纯粹，他能够在一言不发、不加评判的情况下理解她的沉默、渴望和矛盾。对我说来，这正是让他成为不二人选的原因。除了巨大的天赋，库里还能以非凡的喜爱注视着卡尔帕，我觉得这种敏感正是影片中最美好的事物之一。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "影片故事设定在1997年，同时也凸显了厄瓜多尔酷儿群体的一个关键时刻。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“在南部安第斯山区高地奥斯特罗（Austro）地区的保守城市昆卡，警方突袭了在阿巴尼科斯（Abanicos）酒吧举行的一场跨性别选美比赛并逮捕了数人。这一被称为‘阿巴尼科斯之夜’的插曲在我们社群的记忆中留下了深深的创伤，并成为 LGBTIQ+ 人群在我国内地经历迫害与暴力的象征。同年，抗争拉开了序幕。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Nusta_Still3.jpg?w=1024", "alt": "", "caption": "由 Epopeya S.A. 提供", "credit": "Variety · Film", "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Paris-based MMM Film Sales has acquired international rights to Ecuadorian filmmaker Christian Rojas’ debut feature “Princess” (“Ñusta”) ahead of its world premiere at the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival (PÖFF).", "links": [{"text": "MMM Film Sales", "url": "https://variety.com/t/mmm-film-sales/"}, {"text": "Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival", "url": "https://variety.com/t/tallinn-black-nights-film-festival/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“Princess,” which screens in the fest’s First Feature Competition, follows Kallpa, a 12-year-old Indigenous girl from the Andes as she prepares for her community’s festivities, where the ñusta — or princess — is chosen each year. Kallpa dreams of participating but faces a reality: She was born in a boy’s body."}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Related Stories"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/MCDSORE_SP013-e1791584119615.jpg?w=250&h=167&crop=1", "alt": "THE SOCIAL RECKONING, Bill Burr, 2026. © Sony Pictures Releasing / Courtesy Everett Collection", "caption": "", "credit": "Variety · Film"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Bill Burr on ‘The Social Reckoning,’ Sparring With Jeremy Strong as Mark Zuckerberg and Why Tech CEOs are ‘Leading Us to Ruin’", "links": [{"text": "Bill Burr on ‘The Social Reckoning,’ Sparring With Jeremy Strong as Mark Zuckerberg and Why Tech CEOs are ‘Leading Us to Ruin’", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/film/news/bill-burr-the-social-reckoning-zuckerberg-1236907159/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The story explores her search for identity and her gender transition, which are deeply intertwined with her Indigenous roots, her community, and the Andean worldview."}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Popular on Variety"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The film’s “sensory, singular approach to storytelling floored us from the first frames,” says Matthias Angoulvant of MMM Film Sales. “Through the eyes and body of an Indigenous child fighting to exist beyond the identity and role imposed on them, the film renders an intimate pain with extraordinary restraint. A bold, deeply moving queer debut, it embodies the daring cinema we champion at MMM.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“Princess” is produced by Ecuador ’s Epopeya and Oso Rojo Films in co-production with Agua Florida (Peru); Hain Cine (Argentina); Woo Films (Mexico); and Chao Pescao (Bolivia).", "links": [{"text": "Ecuador", "url": "https://variety.com/t/ecuador/"}, {"text": "Woo Films", "url": "https://variety.com/t/woo-films/"}]}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Nusta_Still1.jpg?w=1024", "alt": "", "caption": "Courtesy of Epopeya S.A.", "credit": "Variety · Film"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“For us, more than a business deal, partnering with MMM Film Sales was a meeting of perspectives,” said producer María de los Angeles Palacios of Epopeya. “‘Ñusta’ is a delicate film; it speaks from a place of intimacy, from the body and from a memory that has been silenced.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "She added: “A film like this can’t be taken to market just any way. What makes the difference is that the MMM team understands its gaze and, drawing on their experience, knows how to move it through the international market without stripping away its sensitivity. For a debut feature, having that kind of support matters as much as the visibility itself."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“We always believed the film would find the perfect place to be seen for the first time, and if we’re honest, Tallinn was the one we were hoping for. This year the festival turns 30: It was born in 1997, the same year in which ‘Ñusta’ is set. That coincidence holds a very special meaning for us. That a film shot in the Austro, in Ecuador’s southern Andes, is having its world premiere in Estonia, on the other side of the world, feels both deeply beautiful and paradoxical.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Palacios noted that international interest in Indigenous stories has been growing for years, “and we welcome it. What we hope is that it keeps opening up to how diverse Indigenous peoples and their stories truly are, each with its own language, territory and struggles, and with voices that haven’t always had a space."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“‘Ñusta’ doesn’t try to represent all Indigenous peoples; rather, it draws close to the intimate story of an Andean girl searching for her place in the world. The film was also built through dialogue and a bond with the community that welcomed us. For me, the value of cinema lies precisely in that possibility of approaching other realities with sensitivity, respect and openness, recognizing that there is no single way to tell a story, or to live one.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Indeed, director Rojas stressed the great diversity of Indigenous societies in Ecuador: “It’s important to point out that this film is not about one particular community. In Ecuador there are more than 18 Indigenous peoples and 14 Indigenous nationalities, and they are very diverse. Indigeneity is not one single thing; it is heterogeneous, and this film takes place in the Andes but not in any specific community."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“The process with the community of Sid Sid Anejo, in Cañar, which was our filming location, was fundamental to ‘Ñusta.’ From the start, we wanted to reach out, share the story and listen to them, because it was important to me that the film not arrive in the territory as something foreign, but that it could also be built through the encounter with its people. The most beautiful thing was feeling how they received the story, with so much affection, generosity and openness.”"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Christian-Horizontal.png?w=1024", "alt": "", "caption": "Christian Rojas Courtesy of Oso Rojo Films", "credit": "Variety · Film"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Rojas recalled how, after sharing the story with the community, one of the responses was: “These stories happen, but we don’t talk about them.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“So they decided to give their support. Their involvement went far beyond being in front of the camera: they also got involved behind it and were an active part of building the film as members of the crew,” he added. “Their presence, their trust and the way they accompanied us gave ‘Ñusta’ something that wasn’t only in the script: a life of its own, also born from that encounter. That fills me with immense gratitude."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“I believe cinema also has a responsibility to return to the places and the people who made it possible. That’s why it’s very important to us that, when we release ‘Ñusta’ in Ecuador, we can go back to Sid Sid Anejo and share the film with the community. Not only as a way of thanking them, but because they are also part of this story. It moves me to think that we’ll be able to come together again and watch the film together, in the place where part of it came to life.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "In the film, young KaIlpa embraces her Indigenous identity even as she faces rejection by residents of her village — something that was important for Rojas to portray. “We shouldn’t have to give up one part of who we are in order to live another. Our identity is made of many things: our bodies, the color of our skin, our roots, our desires and the people we love. And all those parts deserve to exist together, without having to ask permission."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“I also wanted to contribute to a more diverse queer representation, one that moves away from stereotypes and recognizes that our experiences are different, that there isn’t just one way of being queer. Indigenous peoples and communities aren’t homogeneous realities either; within them there are voices, struggles and processes of transformation that are opening new paths.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Rojas pointed to Chawpi Runakuna, Ecuador’s first Indigenous LGBTQ collective, which represents several communities in the country. Among its prominent members is Ninari Chimba, an Indigenous lesbian activist who is also part of the film’s cast. “For me, her voice and her struggle are essential, because they remind us that these realities have always existed, even if they often haven’t had a space in which to be expressed,” the director added."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Rojas hoped the film can contribute to greater understanding and acceptance among the more conservative sectors of Ecuadorian society."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“I’d like ‘Ñusta’ to reach those homes too, and those people who still find it hard to understand sexual dissidence. Not through confrontation, but through sensitivity, through encounter and through the possibility of listening to one another."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“I don’t expect everyone who sees the film to think the way I do, but I would like them to be able to get close to Kallpa, get to know her and connect with her story beyond their own beliefs,” Rojas added."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“It moves me to think that the film could open a conversation within a family, that someone might find the courage to listen to their daughter, their son or someone close to them whom they couldn’t understand before. … If the film manages to awaken that sensitivity, even in a single person, I’ll feel that this whole journey has been worth it.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "In making the film, Rojas sought to tell a story not only “about rejection and violence, but also about tenderness, desire, the body, love and the possibility of being free. For me, ‘Ñusta’ isn’t only about what a society can do to a person when it rejects their identity. It’s also about what happens when we find someone who looks at us with love, when we can inhabit our bodies without fear, and when we discover that there is a place in the world where we can be who we are.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Finding the right actor for the part was essential and Rojas succeeded with the casting of the film’s young lead."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“Finding Kuri Fuerez was a marvel. Together with our casting director, Nicolás Yacelga, we met many kids and explored different possibilities for Kallpa, but in Kuri I found something very special. article_text:
Paris-based MMM Film Sales has acquired international rights to Ecuadorian filmmaker Christian Rojas’ debut feature “Princess” (“Ñusta”) ahead of its world premiere at the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival (PÖFF).

“Princess,” which screens in the fest’s First Feature Competition, follows Kallpa, a 12-year-old Indigenous girl from the Andes as she prepares for her community’s festivities, where the ñusta — or princess — is chosen each year. Kallpa dreams of participating but faces a reality: She was born in a boy’s body.

Related Stories

Bill Burr on ‘The Social Reckoning,’ Sparring With Jeremy Strong as Mark Zuckerberg and Why Tech CEOs are ‘Leading Us to Ruin’

The story explores her search for identity and her gender transition, which are deeply intertwined with her Indigenous roots, her community, and the Andean worldview.

Popular on Variety

The film’s “sensory, singular approach to storytelling floored us from the first frames,” says Matthias Angoulvant of MMM Film Sales. “Through the eyes and body of an Indigenous child fighting to exist beyond the identity and role imposed on them, the film renders an intimate pain with extraordinary restraint. A bold, deeply moving queer debut, it embodies the daring cinema we champion at MMM.”

“Princess” is produced by Ecuador ’s Epopeya and Oso Rojo Films in co-production with Agua Florida (Peru); Hain Cine (Argentina); Woo Films (Mexico); and Chao Pescao (Bolivia).

“For us, more than a business deal, partnering with MMM Film Sales was a meeting of perspectives,” said producer María de los Angeles Palacios of Epopeya. “‘Ñusta’ is a delicate film; it speaks from a place of intimacy, from the body and from a memory that has been silenced.”

She added: “A film like this can’t be taken to market just any way. What makes the difference is that the MMM team understands its gaze and, drawing on their experience, knows how to move it through the international market without stripping away its sensitivity. For a debut feature, having that kind of support matters as much as the visibility itself.

“We always believed the film would find the perfect place to be seen for the first time, and if we’re honest, Tallinn was the one we were hoping for. This year the festival turns 30: It was born in 1997, the same year in which ‘Ñusta’ is set. That coincidence holds a very special meaning for us. That a film shot in the Austro, in Ecuador’s southern Andes, is having its world premiere in Estonia, on the other side of the world, feels both deeply beautiful and paradoxical.”

Palacios noted that international interest in Indigenous stories has been growing for years, “and we welcome it. What we hope is that it keeps opening up to how diverse Indigenous peoples and their stories truly are, each with its own language, territory and struggles, and with voices that haven’t always had a space.

“‘Ñusta’ doesn’t try to represent all Indigenous peoples; rather, it draws close to the intimate story of an Andean girl searching for her place in the world. The film was also built through dialogue and a bond with the community that welcomed us. For me, the value of cinema lies precisely in that possibility of approaching other realities with sensitivity, respect and openness, recognizing that there is no single way to tell a story, or to live one.”

Indeed, director Rojas stressed the great diversity of Indigenous societies in Ecuador: “It’s important to point out that this film is not about one particular community. In Ecuador there are more than 18 Indigenous peoples and 14 Indigenous nationalities, and they are very diverse. Indigeneity is not one single thing; it is heterogeneous, and this film takes place in the Andes but not in any specific community.

“The process with the community of Sid Sid Anejo, in Cañar, which was our filming location, was fundamental to ‘Ñusta.’ From the start, we wanted to reach out, share the story and listen to them, because it was important to me that the film not arrive in the territory as something foreign, but that it could also be built through the encounter with its people. The most beautiful thing was feeling how they received the story, with so much affection, generosity and openness.”

Rojas recalled how, after sharing the story with the community, one of the responses was: “These stories happen, but we don’t talk about them.”

“So they decided to give their support. Their involvement went far beyond being in front of the camera: they also got involved behind it and were an active part of building the film as members of the crew,” he added. “Their presence, their trust and the way they accompanied us gave ‘Ñusta’ something that wasn’t only in the script: a life of its own, also born from that encounter. That fills me with immense gratitude.

“I believe cinema also has a responsibility to return to the places and the people who made it possible. That’s why it’s very important to us that, when we release ‘Ñusta’ in Ecuador, we can go back to Sid Sid Anejo and share the film with the community. Not only as a way of thanking them, but because they are also part of this story. It moves me to think that we’ll be able to come together again and watch the film together, in the place where part of it came to life.”

In the film, young KaIlpa embraces her Indigenous identity even as she faces rejection by residents of her village — something that was important for Rojas to portray. “We shouldn’t have to give up one part of who we are in order to live another. Our identity is made of many things: our bodies, the color of our skin, our roots, our desires and the people we love. And all those parts deserve to exist together, without having to ask permission.

“I also wanted to contribute to a more diverse queer representation, one that moves away from stereotypes and recognizes that our experiences are different, that there isn’t just one way of being queer. Indigenous peoples and communities aren’t homogeneous realities either; within them there are voices, struggles and processes of transformation that are opening new paths.”

Rojas pointed to Chawpi Runakuna, Ecuador’s first Indigenous LGBTQ collective, which represents several communities in the country. Among its prominent members is Ninari Chimba, an Indigenous lesbian activist who is also part of the film’s cast. “For me, her voice and her struggle are essential, because they remind us that these realities have always existed, even if they often haven’t had a space in which to be expressed,” the director added.

Rojas hoped the film can contribute to greater understanding and acceptance among the more conservative sectors of Ecuadorian society.

“I’d like ‘Ñusta’ to reach those homes too, and those people who still find it hard to understand sexual dissidence. Not through confrontation, but through sensitivity, through encounter and through the possibility of listening to one another.

“I don’t expect everyone who sees the film to think the way I do, but I would like them to be able to get close to Kallpa, get to know her and connect with her story beyond their own beliefs,” Rojas added.

“It moves me to think that the film could open a conversation within a family, that someone might find the courage to listen to their daughter, their son or someone close to them whom they couldn’t understand before. … If the film manages to awaken that sensitivity, even in a single person, I’ll feel that this whole journey has been worth it.”

In making the film, Rojas sought to tell a story not only “about rejection and violence, but also about tenderness, desire, the body, love and the possibility of being free. For me, ‘Ñusta’ isn’t only about what a society can do to a person when it rejects their identity. It’s also about what happens when we find someone who looks at us with love, when we can inhabit our bodies without fear, and when we discover that there is a place in the world where we can be who we are.”

Finding the right actor for the part was essential and Rojas succeeded with the casting of the film’s young lead.

“Finding Kuri Fuerez was a marvel. Together with our casting director, Nicolás Yacelga, we met many kids and explored different possibilities for Kallpa, but in Kuri I found something very special. He has an extraordinary sensitivity and understanding of the character, as well as tremendous professionalism. What finally convinced me was his ability to understand the story from a very intimate place, to express so many emotions without needing words, simply through a look.

“Kuri didn’t just play Kallpa: He managed to approach her with a tenderness and an honesty that moved me deeply. There was something very genuine in the way he inhabited the character, a way of understanding her silences, her desires and her contradictions without judging her. For me, that’s what made him the right person. Beyond his immense talent, Kuri was able to look at Kallpa with extraordinary affection, and I feel that this sensitivity is one of the most beautiful things living inside the film.”

Set in 1997, the film also highlights a pivotal moment for Ecuador’s queer community.

“In Cuenca, a conservative city in the Austro, Ecuador’s southern Andean region, the police raided a trans beauty pageant being held at the Abanicos bar and arrested several people. That episode, known as ‘The Night of the Abanicos,’ left a deep wound in our community’s memory and became a symbol of the persecution and violence that LGBTIQ+ people lived through in my country. That same year, the struggle began.”

article_text:
Opinion

The Rise and Fall of My Wikipedia Page

After a short entry about me mysteriously appeared, anonymous users debated whether I was credible enough to justify my own page.

Romantic Lowlife Fantasies: Emerging Adults In The Age of Hope in 2021 (all images courtesy Laura June Kirsch)

Back in February, I got a Google Alert that somebody had made a Wikipedia page about me. I immediately texted my mom. She was confused — was it a good thing? Who makes these pages? She’d heard mixed things about Wikipedia.

While her suspicion over enthusiasm was initially disappointing, she had a point. I moved into detective mode and asked a techy friend I had recently met through a cyberpunk friend: “Did you make this?”

He did not. However, he was able to find the source that did, who appeared to be some man who wrote numerous Wikipedia pages mostly about female artists.

The bio he’d written for me was simple: “Laura June Kirsch is an American photographer known for her work documenting music, nightlife and alternative subcultures. In 2021, she published Romantic Lowlife Fantasies: Emerging Adults In The Age of Hope .”

While I was flattered that somebody made the page at all — what artist doesn’t appreciate getting recognition for their work? — I did find it curious how little information was included. Was I supposed to fill in the gaps? How does this work?

Three months later, I received an email from a stranger who runs a digital marketing company with a website that churns out what the kids would call “AI slop.” He wrote that my Wikipedia page had been taken down because it contained too little information and, with his help, the piece could be restored. I was immediately skeptical of him, and while the whole thing was beyond suspect, I was curious. I compiled a robust biography and included a laundry list of links to articles about my work.

article_text:
EXCLUSIVE : Here’s your first trailer for Andrew Haigh ‘s Telluride, Toronto and New York Film Festival drama A Long Winter , starring Fred Hechinger, Ebon Moss-Bachrach, Caitriona Balfe, Kit Connor and D’Pharaoh Woon-A-Tai.

Based on Haigh’s adaptation of Colm Tóibín’s short story of the same name, the film is set during the early 1950s in a remote part of the Colorado mountains “as fall comes to an end and a family prepares for the long winter ahead”.

Pic is produced by Tristan Goligher for The Bureau, Chad Oakes and Mike Frislev for Calgary-based Nomadic Pictures, and Michael Elliott. The film, which plays the London Film Festival this evening, was developed by Mubi and is co-financed by Mubi and Film4. Mubi is handling most of the release with the film in cinemas January 15 in the UK and Ireland, January 22 in the U.S. and Canada, and February 18 in Germany, Austria, Italy, Spain and Latin America.

Haigh’s All of Us Strangers received six BAFTA nominations, including best director and best adapted screenplay for Haigh. It was also the recipient of four Gotham and three Independent Spirit Awards nominations. Haigh’s previous features include Film4-backed Lean on Pete and 45 Years , for which Charlotte Rampling earned an Oscar nomination, and breakout indie hit Weekend .

article_text:
Tom Skerritt, the Emmy-winning actor whose film and television career spanned over six decades, has died at age 93.

Skerritt broke into mainstream prominence with Robert Altman’s M*A*S*H (1970) and early TV guest roles on series like Hawaii Five-O, Gunsmoke and Bonanza . He starred as Captain Dallas in Ridley Scott’s Alien (1979) and Commander “Viper” Metcalf in Top Gun (1986). His wide-ranging film work featured memorable roles in Harold and Maude , Steel Magnolias , A River Runs Through It , Contact , and Bonneville .

RELATED: Tom Skerritt Dies: ‘Top Gun,’ ‘Picket Fences,’ ‘Alien’ Actor Was 93

On television, Skerritt won an Emmy Award as Sheriff Jimmy Brock in the drama Picket Fences and made appearances on shows ranging from Cheers to Madam Secretary .

editorial_excerpt_zh: 武蔵野美術大学 造形構想専攻 映像・写真コースの菅沼比呂志ゼミによる展覧会「写真、その複数形 ～写真をめぐるいくつもの入口」が、武蔵野美術大学市ヶ谷キャンパス1/Mで開催されている。会期は2026年9月26日から1
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "武藏野美术大学造型构想专业影像与摄影方向的菅沼比吕志研讨课展“摄影，其复数形 ～围绕摄影的数个入口”正在武藏野美术大学市谷校区1/M举办。会期为2026年9月26日至10月4日。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "本展共有来自本科四年级、研究生院及博士课程的共计22人参展。年龄层跨度从21岁到35岁不等，其中15人为来自海外的留学生。从大学初学摄影的学生、经由设计等其他领域转向摄影的学生，到有社会人经验后在研究生院重新学习的学生，每人都有着不同的背景。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "正如展览标题中的“复数形”所示，焦点并非单一的摄影观。通过照片、摄影集、屏幕、文字等各种形式，展览从这22人各自的实践出发，重新审视什么是看摄影、通过摄影看什么。展览并非旨在给出完成时的答案，而是将作品比作“句点”“逗号”“问号”“等号”“破折号”，为思考摄影创造出多个“入口”，这正是本次展览的尝试。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "其方法也异彩纷呈。内藤翼的《FACTA》将假新闻与经过物理操作的照片在同一页面上交织，验证了从虚构中生成“现实感”的结构。在包括生成式AI在内、图像的真实性发生动摇的当下，该作品从摄影与媒介双方对“什么是现实，什么是真实”的问题发出了追问。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "另一方面，寺井雅年的《注视的风景》是一件将街头废旧水壶转化为针孔相机的作品。该作品着眼于影像被定型之前的光学现象，构筑成可让观众窥探风景本身在水壶内部倒置投影的形态。这是一次追溯摄影成为“摄影”之前的状态、将媒介原理本身转化为体验的尝试。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "除此之外，学生们的关注点十分广泛，涵盖故乡与土地的历史、记忆、都市、家族、身体、时间等。诸如葛苡辰审视中国东北土地与刻有“满洲”这一名称的历史的《北满之森》、郭晓頴考察在日生活期间自我与场所之间距离的《无法合一》，以及陈泓毅将童年家族照片投影至回忆场所、在单张照片上交织过去与现在的《记忆的印记》等，将摄影限定于“记录”之外的实践排列开来。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "会期尾声还将举办邀请嘉宾的对谈活动。10月3日13点批评家桐折美德、10月4日13点摄影家野口里佳将登台，对学生们的作品进行讲评。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "标题", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "武蔵野美術大学 造形構想専攻 映像・写真コースの菅沼比呂志ゼミによる展覧会「写真、その複数形 ～写真をめぐるいくつもの入口」が、武蔵野美術大学市ヶ谷キャンパス1/Mで開催されている。会期は2026年9月26日から10月4日まで。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "本展には、学部4年生から大学院、博士課程まで計22人が参加。21歳から35歳までと年齢層も幅広く、そのうち15人を海外からの留学生が占める。大学で初めて写真を学んだ学生から、デザインなど別領域を経て写真へと進んだ学生、社会人経験後に大学院で学び直す学生まで、それぞれ異なる背景を持つ。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展覧会のタイトルにある「複数形」が示すように、焦点となるのは単一の写真観ではない。プリント、写真集、スクリーン、言葉などさまざまな形式を通して、写真を見るとは何か、写真を介して何を見るのかを22人それぞれの実践から問い直す。完成された答えを提示するのではなく、作品を「句点」「読点」「クエスチョンマーク」「イコール」「ダッシュ」にたとえながら、写真について考えるための複数の「入口」をつくり出すことが展覧会の試みだ。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "そのアプローチも多岐にわたる。内藤翼の「FACTA」は、フェイクニュースと物理的に操作された写真を同一紙面上で交差させ、虚構から「現実らしさ」が生成される構造を検証。生成AIをはじめイメージの真正性が揺らぐ現在において、「現実とは何か、リアルとは何か」という問題を写真とメディアの双方から問いかける。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "一方、寺井雅也の「注がれた景色」は、街の廃材だったやかんをピンホールカメラへと転換した作品。像が定着される以前の光学現象に着目し、やかんの内部へ反転して投影される風景そのものを鑑賞者が覗き込めるよう構成する。写真が「写真」になる以前の状態へと遡り、メディウムの原理そのものを体験へと変換する試みだ。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "ほかにも、故郷や土地の歴史、記憶、都市、家族、身体、時間など、学生たちの関心は広範囲に及ぶ。中国東北部の土地と「満洲」という名称に刻まれた歴史を見つめる葛苡辰の「北満ノ森」や、日本で暮らすなかで自身と場所との距離を考察する郭暁頴の「ひとつにはならない」、幼少期の家族写真を思い出の場所へ投影し、過去と現在を一枚の写真上で交差させる陳泓毅の「記憶の面影」など、写真を「記録」に限定しない実践が並ぶ。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "会期終盤にはゲストを迎えたトークイベントも実施。10月3日13時から批評家のきりとりめでる、10月4日13時から写真家の野口里佳が登壇し、学生たちの作品について講評する。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "タイトル"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "写真、その複数形 ～写真をめぐるいくつもの入口"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "場所"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "武蔵野美術大学市ヶ谷キャンパス1/M（東京都新宿区市谷田町1-4）"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "会期"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "2026年9月26日（土）～10月4日（日）"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "時間"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "11:00～19:00（最終日は15:00まで）"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "休み"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "無し"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "料金"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "無料"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "新型コロナウイルス感染拡大防止のため、当サイトに掲載している展覧会やイベントの内容が変更になっている可能性があります。公式サイトなどから最新情報をご確認ください。"}]
article_text:
武蔵野美術大学 造形構想専攻 映像・写真コースの菅沼比呂志ゼミによる展覧会「写真、その複数形 ～写真をめぐるいくつもの入口」が、武蔵野美術大学市ヶ谷キャンパス1/Mで開催されている。会期は2026年9月26日から10月4日まで。

本展には、学部4年生から大学院、博士課程まで計22人が参加。21歳から35歳までと年齢層も幅広く、そのうち15人を海外からの留学生が占める。大学で初めて写真を学んだ学生から、デザインなど別領域を経て写真へと進んだ学生、社会人経験後に大学院で学び直す学生まで、それぞれ異なる背景を持つ。

展覧会のタイトルにある「複数形」が示すように、焦点となるのは単一の写真観ではない。プリント、写真集、スクリーン、言葉などさまざまな形式を通して、写真を見るとは何か、写真を介して何を見るのかを22人それぞれの実践から問い直す。完成された答えを提示するのではなく、作品を「句点」「読点」「クエスチョンマーク」「イコール」「ダッシュ」にたとえながら、写真について考えるための複数の「入口」をつくり出すことが展覧会の試みだ。

そのアプローチも多岐にわたる。内藤翼の「FACTA」は、フェイクニュースと物理的に操作された写真を同一紙面上で交差させ、虚構から「現実らしさ」が生成される構造を検証。生成AIをはじめイメージの真正性が揺らぐ現在において、「現実とは何か、リアルとは何か」という問題を写真とメディアの双方から問いかける。

一方、寺井雅也の「注がれた景色」は、街の廃材だったやかんをピンホールカメラへと転換した作品。像が定着される以前の光学現象に着目し、やかんの内部へ反転して投影される風景そのものを鑑賞者が覗き込めるよう構成する。写真が「写真」になる以前の状態へと遡り、メディウムの原理そのものを体験へと変換する試みだ。

ほかにも、故郷や土地の歴史、記憶、都市、家族、身体、時間など、学生たちの関心は広範囲に及ぶ。中国東北部の土地と「満洲」という名称に刻まれた歴史を見つめる葛苡辰の「北満ノ森」や、日本で暮らすなかで自身と場所との距離を考察する郭暁頴の「ひとつにはならない」、幼少期の家族写真を思い出の場所へ投影し、過去と現在を一枚の写真上で交差させる陳泓毅の「記憶の面影」など、写真を「記録」に限定しない実践が並ぶ。

会期終盤にはゲストを迎えたトークイベントも実施。10月3日13時から批評家のきりとりめでる、10月4日13時から写真家の野口里佳が登壇し、学生たちの作品について講評する。

タイトル

写真、その複数形 ～写真をめぐるいくつもの入口

場所

武蔵野美術大学市ヶ谷キャンパス1/M（東京都新宿区市谷田町1-4）

会期

2026年9月26日（土）～10月4日（日）

時間

11:00～19:00（最終日は15:00まで）

休み

無し

料金

無料

article_text:
関西の秋の恒例行事「関西文化の日」が、今年も11月に開催される。関西一円の美術館・博物館・資料館などが参加し、入館料（原則として常設展）を無料とする取り組みである。2026年は、11月14日〜15日を中心日として実施。参加施設は各館の都合に合わせて11月中の特定日に無料開放を設定する。京都・大阪・兵庫をはじめ、滋賀、奈良、和歌山など関西広域にわたる数百の文化施設が参加予定で、例年どおり多様なコレクションが市民に開かれることになる。各館の無料開放日や展示情報は こちら からチェック可能。

本記事では、その中から編集部が注目する12館をピックアップ！ 各地の美術館や博物館をめぐりながら、関西の文化の現在地を体感してみてはいかがだろうか。

【京都】 京都国立近代美術館 ：11月15日

京都を中心に、関西・西日本の美術を軸とした収集・研究・展示を行う。陶芸、漆芸、染織などの工芸分野に力を入れており、所蔵品は1万3千点を超える。コレクションギャラリーでは、企画展にあわせて年数回の展示替えを行い、多彩な作品を紹介している。 無料となる展示内容：コレクション展

コレクション展：「2026年度 第3回コレクション展」

電話：075-761-4111 https://www.momak.go.jp/

【京都】 京都国際マンガミュージアム ：11月25日

京都市と京都精華大学が運営する、日本初のマンガ総合文化施設。江戸期の戯画や浮世絵から、明治・大正・昭和の雑誌、戦後の貸本、現代の人気作、海外作品まで、約30万点の資料を所蔵し公開している。 無料となる展示内容：全館（有料イベント等を除く）

【京都】 京都市京セラ美術館 ：11月14日〜15日

近現代の京都の美術を中心に、日本画、洋画、彫刻、工芸、書、版画など約4500点を所蔵する。建築家・青木淳と西澤徹夫によるリノベーションで蘇った歴史的建築が印象的で、7代目小川治兵衛が手がけたとされる日本庭園も見どころである。 無料となる展示内容：コレクション展

【大阪】 堺 アルフォンス・ミュシャ館 ：11月17日

アルフォンス・ミュシャの初期から晩年期にまでわたる作品を展示し、生涯にわたる創作活動を紹介している。ミュシャの作品はしなやかな曲線と美しい色彩が特徴で、異国趣味や古典古代を思わせる装飾様式のほか、日本など東洋の美術の要素もみられ、『明星』や『みだれ髪』などを通じて日本にも大きな影響を及ぼした。 無料となる展示内容：企画展 企画展：「ミュシャ芸術博覧会リターンズ」

【滋賀】 滋賀県立美術館 ：11月14日〜15日

1984年に開館し、びわこ文化公園の中に位置する滋賀県立美術館は、2021年のリニューアルでショップやカフェ、キッズスペースなどを備え、誰もが立ち寄れる開かれた場所へと生まれ変わった。近代日本画や滋賀ゆかりの作家、現代美術、アール・ブリュットなど多彩なコレクションを通じて、地域と表現をつなぐ場となっている。 無料となる展示内容：常設展

滋賀県近江八幡市、伝統的建造物群保存地区の町並みに溶け込むように佇む美術館。昭和初期の町家を改装した空間で、障がいのある人たちの造形表現や現代アートなど、多様な表現を分け隔てなく紹介している。 無料となる展示内容：コレクション展 コレクション展：「NO-MAコレクションPart 5 『NO-MAヒストリー』」

【兵庫】 兵庫県立美術館 ：11月14日〜15日

阪神・淡路大震災からの「文化の復興」を掲げ、2002年に開館。前身の近代美術館時代から続く約半世紀の収集活動により、現在は1万点を超える作品を所蔵する。建築は安藤忠雄による設計で、海に面したダイナミックな構造が特徴である。 無料となる展示内容：常設展

美術と歴史の両部門を備える複合施設で、芦屋ゆかりの作家による作品をはじめ、近現代美術、地域の自然や歴史に関する文化財と考古資料を収集・研究している。
